t: Nothing in this Act or any amendment made by this Act may be construed to affect or limit the application of or obligation to comply with any environmental law, including section 120(h) of the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act of 1980 (42 U.S.C. 9620(h)).

fable.w: This is a savings clause that preserves the application of existing environmental laws, including CERCLA section 120(h). The tempting reading is that environmental laws often carry public comment or state consultation requirements, but this section does not itself create or require any consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving parties outside the federal government. It only says the Act does not alter existing obligations.
fable.s: Nothing in this Act or any amendment made by this Act may be construed to affect or limit the application of or obligation to comply with any environmental law

opus.w: This is a savings clause: it only says the Act does not weaken existing environmental laws. It creates no comment period, hearing, rulemaking, consultation with states or the public, advisory body, or right to sue. It is tempting to say the clause brings in the participation steps of other laws, but simply naming another statute does not set up any process for outsiders to take part in a federal decision.
opus.s: Nothing in this Act or any amendment made by this Act may be construed to affect or limit the application of or obligation to comply with any environmental law
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** This clause keeps environmental laws like CERCLA in force, and some of those laws have their own public-comment or consultation steps. So one might think it brings in participation.

   **Why that fails:** The section only says this Act doesn't weaken laws that already exist. It does not itself require any comment period, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. Section 120(h) of CERCLA, the law it names, deals with notices and covenants when federal property is transferred, not with public participation.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a savings clause that preserves the applicability of other environmental laws. It does not itself require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties. Merely referencing another statute that might contain participation requirements does not make this section a participation requirement.
qwen_chat.s: Nothing in this Act or any amendment made by this Act may be construed to affect or limit the application of or obligation to comply with any environmental law, including section 120(h) of the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act of 1980 (42 U.S.C. 9620(h)).
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that referencing "section 120(h) of CERCLA" implies participation because that specific section of CERCLA involves consultation with states and tribes. However, this section merely states that the current Act does not override existing laws; it does not itself mandate or describe any participatory process. It is a savings clause, not a procedural requirement for participation within this statute.
